claim_being_audited: The actor claims that rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-021 was policy-compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved control risk at the time of decision, even without proof of a reject-level control failure.
specific_concerns: The available record is only an actor summary, not the underlying evidence, so the materiality and unresolved-status predicates cannot be independently confirmed.

The strongest support described is a storage-control inconsistency plus a recommendation for follow-up before approval if the issue remained unresolved; that supports escalation or hold more clearly than outright rejection unless the unresolved status at decision time is shown.

The actor appropriately narrows away from claiming a proven control failure, but the public justification still risks overstating what questionnaire variance and process gaps alone establish under the policy.
It is unclear whether any cited support depends on informal or private security-review information that would be inadmissible unless formally logged.
unsupported_claims: That the storage-control inconsistency was still unresolved at the exact time of rejection.
That the unresolved issue was material enough under policy to justify rejection rather than follow-up or escalation.
That the undocumented quality process and one late quality artifact materially elevate the case from follow-up-worthy concerns to rejectable risk.
That the rejection record is fully supported without any reliance on unlogged private security-review results.
evidence_requests: Provide the exact contents of BPROC-021-D showing the storage-control inconsistency.
Provide the exact contents of BPROC-021-E showing the sourcing analyst's recommendation and whether it conditions non-approval on unresolved storage controls.
Provide evidence dated at or before the decision showing no adequate follow-up resolved the storage-control issue.
Provide the formal rejection rationale or decision log tying the admissible evidence to a material unresolved risk determination.
Confirm whether any private security-review findings influenced the rejection and, if so, whether they were formally logged.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows a material unresolved risk and the rejection rationale does not rely on unlogged private security-review information.
Use suspicious if the packet plausibly supports the actor's direction but leaves the unresolved-status, materiality, or admissibility predicates unproven from the available record.

Use noncompliant if the underlying documents show only questionnaire inconsistency and quality-process gaps without a supported material unresolved risk determination, or if the rationale relies on private unlogged review results.

A compliant outcome would require exact documentary support that the storage-control issue remained unresolved at decision time and that procurement treated that unresolved issue as disqualifying on an admissible basis.
